# Results — Study 657 (Larry Portfolio)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One recipe — hold a fixed
**30% IJS (small-cap value) / 70% IEF (7-10y Treasuries)** blend, **rebalanced on the first
trading day of each year** (drift in between), charge **2 bps** one-way on rebalance
turnover — run on the **total-return** tapes and pinned against a fixed **60% SPY / 40% IEF**
(the same construction as sibling study
[97-balancing-act](../97-balancing-act/docs/results.md)), 100% stocks (SPY), 100% small-value
(IJS) and 100% bonds (IEF) alone. Sharpes are **excess-of-cash** (SHY, 1-3y Treasuries) so
every race compares excess-of-cash to excess-of-cash. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete
calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Joint fingerprint `8940a2d59087`.*

## Does Larry match 60/40's RETURN? — no, and it's certified

| Quantity | Value |
|---|--:|
| CAGR gap (Larry − 60/40) | **−2.66 pts/yr** |
| Mean-return difference (bootstrap point) | **−2.75%/yr** |
| 95% bootstrap CI (circular block, 21d, 2,000 reps) | **[−4.92%, −0.52%]** — excludes 0 |
| HAC *t* on the daily (Larry − 60/40) return difference | **−2.29** (\|t\| ≥ 2) |

The "60/40-like returns" promise is **not kept** on this tape: Larry trails a free 60/40 by
a certified **−2.66 pts/yr**, and the gap clears the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar both as a Newey-West
statistic and as a bootstrap CI that sits entirely below zero.

## Is the RISK-ADJUSTED (Sharpe) edge real? — no, it's a statistical tie

| Quantity | Value |
|---|--:|
| Sharpe (xs) gap (Larry − 60/40) | **−0.050** |
| Bootstrap Sharpe-diff point | −0.050 |
| 95% bootstrap CI (circular block, 21d, 2,000 reps) | **[−0.292, +0.187]** — includes 0 |
| Larry wins the Sharpe race in … of resamples | 32% |

Unlike the raw return gap, the risk-adjusted comparison is **not distinguishable from zero**
— Larry's much smaller equity sleeve buys back most, but not certifiably all, of its return
shortfall in reduced volatility.

## The equity-risk claim — real, and doesn't need a t-stat

| Metric | Larry | 60/40 | 100% SPY |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Annualised vol | **7.1%** | 10.2% | 18.8% |
| Max drawdown | **−20.8%** | −29.8% | −55.2% |
| Daily correlation to SPY | **0.57** | 0.96 | 1.00 |

This part of the pitch is simply true by construction — running 30% small-value equity
instead of 60% broad-market equity mechanically halves the correlation to a pure-equity
crash and cuts both volatility and drawdown by roughly a third. No inference needed; it's
arithmetic on the weights.

## Third axis — has the small-value premium (IJS − SPY) itself decayed?

| Era | Annualised spread | *n* (days) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Whole sample (2002 → 2026) | **+0.15%/yr** | 6,017 | **+0.06** |
| 2002 → 2007 (pre-split) | +5.08%/yr | 1,114 | +1.20 |
| 2007 → 2026 (post-split) | **−0.97%/yr** | 4,903 | −0.35 |
| Welch *t* of the difference (late − early) | | | **−1.11** |

Split at **2007-01-01** — externally justified, not snooped: AQR (Asness, Frazzini, Israel &
Moskowitz, 2015, *Fact, Fiction and Value Investing*) and Swedroe's own later writing both
date the value factor's well-documented drawdown to the years following the Global Financial
Crisis. Neither era's premium is individually significant, and the era **difference** is not
certified either (*t* = −1.11) — but the whole-sample premium is itself statistically
indistinguishable from zero (*t* = +0.06). The honest reading is not "the premium existed and
decayed" so much as **"this 24-year ETF tape never showed a certifiable small-value premium
in the first place"** — consistent with siblings
[513-size-effect](../513-size-effect/docs/results.md) and
[530-book-to-market-value](../530-book-to-market-value/docs/results.md), which find the same
absence on different modern baskets.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic 3-asset (MKT, SV, BOND) world, CAPM-neutral (`beta_sv = 1.0`) by construction,
with a TUNABLE planted small-value premium; no network. The pass/fail target is the
premium-detection statistic itself (HAC *t* on the SV − MKT spread) — the same primitive the
third axis applies to the real IJS − SPY tape.

| World | Premium HAC *t* | Premium recovered |
|---|--:|--:|
| null (premium = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **+0.01** (sd 1.06), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 1/20 seeds** | — |
| planted premium = +5.0%/yr (seed 657) | **+2.79** | +6.71%/yr |

At premium = 0 the Larry-vs-60/40 CAGR gap still averages **−1.23 pts/yr** across the 20
null seeds — the *structural* cost of running far less equity beta (30% × β1.0 vs 60% × β1.0),
not a detector failure; it is the same mechanical fact measured on the real tape above. Once a
genuine premium is planted (+5.0%/yr), the detector recovers it cleanly (*t* = +2.79) and the
portfolio-level CAGR gap flips positive (**+2.55 pts/yr**, Larry Sharpe 0.686 vs 60/40 0.290)
— proof the machinery *can* find a real premium and correctly attribute the portfolio-level
consequence; it simply doesn't find one on the real 2002–2026 tape. *(A faithful-engine /
power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — MIXED.** *Real* on the risk cut (mechanical: vol 7.1% vs 10.2%, maxDD −20.8% vs
  −29.8%, correlation to SPY 0.57 vs 0.96) · *None* on the "delivers 60/40-like returns"
  claim (CAGR **−2.66 pts/yr**, HAC *t* = **−2.29**, bootstrap CI **[−4.92%, −0.52%]**
  excludes zero) · risk-adjusted (Sharpe) comparison is a **statistical tie** (CI
  **[−0.292, +0.187]** includes zero, Larry wins only 32% of resamples).
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** Two cheap, liquid ETFs, low turnover (annual rebalance, 2 bps)
  — genuinely easy to run. But it certifiably underperformed a free 60/40 on this tape, and
  the rationale that would make that acceptable — a persistent small-value premium — is
  statistically indistinguishable from zero on the only window this data allows (*t* = +0.06
  whole-sample).
- **"Has the small-value premium decayed since popularization?" — MIXED.** Can't certify
  decay (era-difference *t* = −1.11) — but can't certify the premium was ever robustly
  present on this modern ETF tape either. Both eras are individually insignificant.
